title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic generate→verify→repair guard increases deterministic-verifier semantic correctness for translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents sampled from a deterministic task generator spanning four intent families, shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, at most one repair allowed per intent. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Only one guarded repair was invoked; provider-call audit: model_calls_used = 151; completed_episode_count = 300. Interpretation: on this synthetic verifier-capable corpus, the guarded workflow yielded a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We report concrete execution accounting, statistical diagnostics, and reproducibility artifacts, and we recommend baseline-calibration pilots and explicit generation-semantic choices for future preregistered NetOps trials.

sections.introduction: Natural-language intent interfaces offer to simplify NetOps by letting operators specify changes in free text that are translated automatically into device-level configurations. Prior work shows that single-pass LLM outputs commonly include syntactic errors, omissions, or semantics that violate operator invariants, motivating guarded pipelines that verify and repair candidate outputs before deployment [1][2][3]. We studied whether a constrained prompt format plus an automated deterministic verifier and a single allowed repair call materially improves verifier-level semantic correctness relative to a baseline free-text prompting condition. The trial was preregistered (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) and executed with full artifactization and provider auditing. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory trial with deterministic-verifier endpoints on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150); (2) an artifact-grounded quantitative outcome showing a negligible guarded-vs-baseline improvement (149→150 correct; p=1.0; 95% CI [0.00,0.02]); and (3) methodological recommendations arising from the observed ceiling effect, including baseline-calibration pilots and explicit declaration of generation semantics.
sections.related_work: Three research strands motivate this study. First, intent-to-configuration work documents low-to-moderate NL→formal translation accuracy in many benchmarks and argues for post-generation checks [1][2]. Second, generate→verify→repair architectures—ranging from verifier-in-the-loop fine-tuning to runtime repair policies—have shown improvements for infrastructure-as-code and configuration repair tasks, with effect size dependent on repair budgets, sampling semantics, and baseline model competence [4][7]. Third, security analyses show that unchecked LLM outputs in multi-tool agents can convert false textual claims into harmful actions, arguing for deterministic gating and auditable traces [6][8]. Our trial differs from many prior evaluations by (a) using explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial sampled candidate shared across baseline and guarded), (b) enforcing a strict one-repair budget, and (c) measuring a deterministic verifier pass/fail endpoint on a synthetic, verifier-capable corpus restricted to small topologies. These design choices define a narrow estimand—marginal value of a one-repair guard applied to an identical initial sample—distinct from independent-sampling or multi-repair estimands reported elsewhere.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study preregistration (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) froze the design, estimands, inclusion/exclusion rules, and analysis plan before any model interactions. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline measured via an exact two-sided McNemar test on paired verifier pass/fail outcomes. The confirmatory sample size N=150 was chosen to detect an absolute +15 percentage-point improvement with ≈80% power under conservative discordant-pair assumptions; this target is reported because the observed baseline invalidated that assumption.

Execution semantics and sampling. The execution adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial model generation was sampled and that identical candidate was used to evaluate both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline could invoke at most one repair call only if the deterministic validator failed the initial shared candidate. This semantics isolates the marginal effect of applying a single repair to the same first-pass output; it does not estimate the effect of per-condition independent draws or of re-sampling multiple initial candidates per condition. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). Because no numeric temperature or fixed random seed was enforced (temperature = null), model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions; this explicit runtime-sampling fact is recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and is stated here to resolve sampling-parameter ambiguity.

Task bank, generator, and verifier coverage. Confirmatory tasks (N=150) were deterministically generated by the preregistered generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and span four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topologies were limited to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes) per the preregistration. Pre-execution mapping and verifier-coverage unit-tests ran and passed; no confirmatory exclusions were necessary. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule returning boolean pass/fail plus normalized final-configuration text and diagnostic fields (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). Validator inputs, validation_before/after traces, and normalized_configuration strings were archived for every episode.

Adapter enforcement, retries, and contamination controls. The execution contract (adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1) enforced one initial generation per task and at most one repair invocation. Provider-call auditing recorded model_calls_used = 151 (150 shared_initial generations + 1 repair), completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, and cache_miss_count = 151. Stage_counts recorded shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. Inclusion/exclusion rules (deterministic ambiguity detector, parser mapping failures, verifier unsupported-feature flags) were applied deterministically pre-execution; none occurred for the confirmatory set. The preregistered missingness policy specified one automatic retry on provider timeouts then mark failed; no retries were required because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0.

Scoring and inferential procedures. Primary outcome: deterministic verifier pass/fail per episode. Primary analysis: exact two-sided McNemar test applied to the paired contingency counts, plus a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration specified exclusion of incomplete pairs for the primary test (complete_pair_primary). Secondary contrasts and multiplicity correction plans were preregistered but constrained by the enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and the one-repair budget; these constraints are reported and adhered to.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 (150 tasks × 2 conditions) and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider-call audit: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts: shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 1. Contamination checks and mapping unit-tests passed; contamination_summary.csv is empty.

Primary numerical outcomes (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is n_11 = 149, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Per-condition success counts: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). These numbers are reproduced directly from analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and iteration distribution. Only one guarded repair was invoked (1/150 episodes), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. The single repair converted one initially failing candidate into a verifier-valid configuration. Summary statistics: median revision iterations in guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces (validation_before and validation_after) for representative tasks (task-000001—task-000006) are archived and show differing difficulty labels (medium, hard, very_hard) with parsed_command_count and required_command_count consistent with task payloads.

Representative example. Task-000001 intent: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up. Do not modify any other interface." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence. Validator diagnostics for task-000001: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, valid = true. Representative response and scorer traces are archived (execution/responses and execution/scoring entries) and reproduces the normalized_configuration string used by the verifier.

Sensitivity and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not invoked because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No parser failures, unsupported-feature exclusions, or ambiguity-driven exclusions occurred in the confirmatory set.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation and ceiling effect. The observed baseline rate (149/150 ≈ 99.33%) left little headroom for a one-repair guarded policy to demonstrate a large absolute improvement. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline (target detectable +15 percentage points), so the realized high baseline renders the confirmatory power target uninformative. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 and narrow bootstrap CI [0.00,0.02] indicate that any marginal guarded improvement on this corpus is bounded to at most a few percentage points under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget.

Methodological implications: generation semantics and operational estimands. Shared_initial_candidate semantics make the baseline measurement the validity of the single first-sampled candidate; the guarded condition isolates the incremental value of applying a repair to that same candidate. Independent per-condition sampling or re-sampling multiple initial candidates per condition estimate a different operational quantity (average per-condition performance across independent draws) and can yield larger observable gains when sampling variance is substantial. Practitioners designing trials or production pipelines must select generation semantics that reflect operational behavior (e.g., whether a deployed system will re-sample alternatives or apply repairs to a fixed first-pass output).

Operational affordances beyond verifier pass/fail. Even when marginal verifier-pass gains are numerically small on constrained corpora, guarded workflows provide operational benefits not captured by a binary endpoint: (1) deterministic normalized configurations and validation traces that are auditable for operator review; (2) concise violation codes and parsed_command_count fields that accelerate triage; and (3) explicit repair prompts and repair traces that support incident post-mortem. These affordances—present in our archived validator traces—can justify guarded pipelines operationally even when absolute pass-rate gains are limited.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: adapter-enforced call budgets, fresh API sessions per call, and provider-call auditing mitigate leakage; however, shared_initial_candidate semantics purposely reduce sampling variance and therefore do not reflect independent-sampling scenarios. Construct validity: deterministic verifier pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; mapping unit-tests mitigated but do not eliminate residual mapping risk. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic tasks, and small topologies (4–32 nodes); we do not claim generalization to production-scale WANs or vendor-heterogeneous CLIs. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumptions were invalidated by the high baseline, reducing confirmatory interpretability for large effect sizes.

Recommendations for future preregistered NetOps trials. (1) Run a short baseline-calibration pilot (20–40 tasks) sampled from the planned generator and prompt style to estimate baseline competence and adjust N or task difficulty before confirmatory sampling. (2) Explicitly preregister generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent-sampling) because they change the estimand. (3) Include repair-budget sensitivity arms (multiple allowed repairs) to estimate diminishing returns. (4) Test model diversity (multiple model families/sizes) and explicit sampling parameters (set numeric temperature and fixed seeds when determinism is required). (5) Incrementally scale topology size and verifier coverage while validating mapping-tool correctness with unit-tests prior to batch execution. These recommendations follow directly from the execution accounting, analysis artifacts, and the ceiling effect observed in our run.

Reproducibility and artifact availability. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest. Key reproducible parameters: bootstrap_seed = 1729, bootstrap_resamples = 10000, model_calls_used = 151, completed_episode_count = 300, complete_pair_count = 150, repair invocations = 1, declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", validator_id = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5" (version 5.0), task generator id = "deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5". The analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, analysis_log.jsonl) reproduce the numeric results reported above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired trial comparing unconstrained baseline prompting to constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a synthetic verifier-capable corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically small and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The main scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials benefit from baseline-calibration pilots and explicit generation-semantic declarations to avoid ceiling effects and to align estimands with operational behavior. Future work should evaluate independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, multiple models, and scaled verifier coverage; our archived artifacts provide a reproducible baseline and concrete operational diagnostics to guide those efforts.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across other model families or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and repair budget: execution enforced a single shared initial candidate per task and at most one repair invocation; different generation semantics or larger repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: observed baseline correctness (149/150) was far higher than the preregistered power assumption (target detectable +15 percentage points), reducing confirmatory power and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and mapping risk: the deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; mapping unit-tests mitigated but cannot fully eliminate residual translation risks.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not assess adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to evaluate claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
